sections.html:
Four offices each keep a piece of your file. The county Property Appraiser describes the parcel, the county Tax Collector sends the bill, the Clerk and Comptroller stores the recorded deed, and the city Building Department holds permits. Once an offer lands, knowing that split saves a lot of repeat phone calls.

You can list the house, sell it privately or deal directly with a cash buyer. A listing reaches the most people but comes with open houses and punch lists. A direct purchase gives up some price for fewer moving parts, and you name the closing date.

  • Print the parcel record before anyone tours the house.
  • Request old permit files and final inspections from the city.
  • Ask each lender for a written payoff figure.

sections.h2: An older city and what buyers check
sections.html:
Boynton Beach started as a small settlement and became the Town of Boynton on April 14, 1920. After a century of growth, you find mid-century blocks next to newer subdivisions, and buyers price the two very differently.

Older houses invite inspection requests. The city runs a permit history service with building plans, site plans, applications, certificates of occupancy and elevation certificates for addresses inside city limits. If an earlier owner added a screen room, replaced a roof or changed an electrical panel, that file shows whether the job was closed out. An open permit is far easier to settle before you sign a contract than in the middle of a buyer's inspection period.

For the year a house was built, the city points people to the Property Appraiser, so a buyer's agent will probably look there first.

sections.h2: Can the new HB 803 permit exemption help before listing?
sections.html:
It may help, depending on the job. House Bill 803 took effect July 1, 2026 and created two permit exemptions for single family homes. Boynton Beach set up a request process in its online permitting portal.

The first exemption covers small jobs valued under $7,500. You send the Building Department a written request with a contract or other proof of the work's scope and value. Staff then issue a written determination or tell you to apply for a permit. Cutting one project into pieces to stay under the cap is not allowed.

The city is firm about the limits. Structural, electrical, mechanical, plumbing and gas work still needs a permit at any price, and so does any work on a property in a flood hazard area. Fences and driveways stay under the zoning code. The second exemption covers temporary flood panels or barriers put in by a state-certified contractor, and it also leaves out flood hazard areas. For both, the city says it owes no legal duty to owners or later buyers for exempted work.

  • Described as fine: interior trim, flooring, replacing cabinets, sinks and light fixtures, repairing drywall.
  • Described as still permitted: moving sinks or water heaters, tub to shower conversions, windows, doors, shutters, garage or patio conversions.

Exempt work gets no city inspection, so keep receipts and photos to hand to the buyer.

sections.h2: Common code violations to fix before photos
sections.html:
The city's list of repeat offenders is mostly cheap to correct before you take listing photos.

  • Grass taller than nine inches, or dead sod that has not been replaced.
  • House numbers missing from the building itself. They must be at least four inches tall and contrast with the wall.
  • Peeling paint, damaged fascia, loose awnings or broken screen enclosures.
  • Inoperable or unregistered vehicles, appliances and household items stored outside.
  • Construction debris over three cubic yards, which needs a special pickup from Public Works.

Boats and recreational vehicles may sit on a driveway, in a carport or in the rear yard if a resident owns them, they are registered, and no repair work lasts more than seven days. Nobody may live in a parked RV on private land unless zoning allows it.

Landlords should also know the city bars leasing any residential unit without a business tax receipt and a certificate of use and occupancy for that unit. If you are selling a rented house, confirm both were in place, since a buyer's lender or title agent may ask.

sections.h2: What is the Super Senior exemption?
sections.html:
Boynton Beach and Delray Beach are the only two cities named on the appraiser's exemption chart for a Super Senior exemption. It removes the city's own levies, not the county, school or other bills.

To qualify, an owner must meet the limited-income senior rules, have owned and lived in the home as a permanent residence for at least 25 years, and hold a property with market value under $250,000 at application. A long-time owner who has it should say so plainly to a buyer, because the benefit belongs to the owner and does not pass with the house.

Exemptions on the appraiser's chart most relevant to sellers

The senior exemption also has a 2026 household income limit. Read it on the appraiser's site before you apply.

Three statewide rules matter most. A conveyance of land needs a signed writing with two witnesses, and the witnessing may be done over audio-video link. The stamp tax is seventy cents per hundred dollars here, and everyone named on the deed answers for it. And the Clerk collects that tax when the deed is recorded, along with page-based fees under section 28.24.

Ask your closing agent for the draft settlement statement before signing day, since it should itemize all three. Using a quitclaim form does not avoid the tax when money or a mortgage is part of the deal.

sections.h2: Your tax bill and homestead after a sale
sections.html:
The closing agent settles the bill for the year of sale at the table and pays any open balance from your proceeds. The buyer's assessment returns to market value the January after closing.

The savings you built up under the cap follow you only if you file for portability when you claim a new Florida homestead. Renting out the home or moving away ends the exemption, so avoid placing a tenant while you wait to close. Owners with limited income may ask the Tax Collector about the deferral program, which uses Form DR-570.

A short list keeps a quick sale from stalling. Confirm every owner on title can sign. Gather the deed, the latest tax bill and any lease. Get payoff letters in writing. Ask the title agent how prorations will be handled. If a buyer's side asks for repairs, answer in writing and keep a copy. After closing, forward your mail and cancel services effective the day the deed is recorded, and keep the settlement statement with your tax records.

faqs.q: Where can I see what work was permitted on my Boynton Beach house?
faqs.a: The city's permit history service holds plans, applications, certificates of occupancy and elevation certificates for properties in city limits. Request your address file before you list, and use the Property Appraiser's record for the year built.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to swap kitchen cabinets before a sale?
faqs.a: Often not, under the city's HB 803 guidance, if the job is under $7,500 and involves no plumbing, electrical, structural, mechanical or gas work. You must file a written exemption request, and flood hazard area properties are excluded.

faqs.q: Can a Boynton Beach landlord sell a rented house?
faqs.a: Yes, but confirm the city business tax receipt and certificate of use and occupancy were in place for the unit. A buyer or title agent may ask for them.

faqs.q: Does the Super Senior exemption transfer to the buyer?
faqs.a: No. It is tied to the owner's 25 years of residence and income filing, so the next owner starts fresh and is assessed at full value after the next January 1.

faqs.q: Who collects the deed stamp tax on a Boynton Beach sale?
faqs.a: The Palm Beach County Clerk collects it at recording, and the sales contract decides which side pays. Ask your closing agent to show the figure on the draft settlement statement.
